page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is an entry-level, shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a 1/2 shared physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the e2-medium is designed for light, non-continuous workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is rated as average, while multi-core performance falls into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with uncached read and write speeds of 6.36 GB/sec and 4.83 GB/sec respectively, placing it in the bottom tier of tested hardware. Geekbench scores reflect similar limits, with single-core and multi-core scores both in the bottom 10 percent, and static web serving throughput measured at 0.63 GB/sec.

From a resource density and cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-medium offers a low-cost entry point for hosting basic services by utilizing a shared-core CPU allocation. The primary tradeoff is the potential for CPU scheduling latency and limited throughput under sustained multi-threaded execution, as evidenced by its low Passmark database operations score of 884.33 and weak multi-core performance.

This instance is best suited for lightweight, bursty, or development workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale web serving, development and testing environments, basic text processing, and running small utility scripts or microservices that do not require sustained high CPU or memory bandwidth.
